It implements a file-backed virtual block device that automatically performs compression and encryption as blocks are accessed without requiring root privileges.Why it’s interestingIt provides a live compressed, encrypted archive using custom 32-bit arithmetic encoding, ChaCha20-Poly1305 encryption, and CRC8 plus XOR parity error-correction with minimal dependencies.Source metrics: Points 2 · Comments 0HN discussion · ProjectSource: #HackerNews / Show HN
items.content_html:
🛠️ Lightweight FUSE-based encrypted, compressed filesystem for Linux

Summary
ObFUSEcate is a lightweight FUSE-based encrypted and compressed filesystem for Linux written in C++. It implements a file-backed virtual block device that automatically performs compression and encryption as blocks are accessed without requiring root privileges.

Why it’s interesting
It provides a live compressed, encrypted archive using custom 32-bit arithmetic encoding, ChaCha20-Poly1305 encryption, and CRC8 plus XOR parity error-correction with minimal dependencies.
